subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: After the persistence-ordering defect is repaired, should OpenClaw accept `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` and the generic synchronous `onTaskTimeout` queue callback as permanent supported contracts?
rationale: The defect has a mechanical repair, but whether to add a new operator setting and generic queue API is a compatibility and ownership choice that source correctness alone cannot settle.

options.title: Accept both contracts
options.body: Land the opt-in config and generic hook after the persistence settlement barrier and regression are added.

options.title: Keep the hook internal
options.body: Preserve the timeout behavior but replace the generic callback with a maintenance-owned release/fence mechanism to avoid expanding queue API.

options.title: Reuse existing timeout policy
options.body: Avoid the new config and bind maintenance through an existing host safety timeout if maintainers prefer one canonical operator policy.

recommendation.title: Accept both contracts
recommendation.body: Land the opt-in config and generic hook after the persistence settlement barrier and regression are added.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work spans all three decision surfaces: deferred maintenance, transcript rewrite, and command-queue timeout semantics.
